summary.headline: Prostarm Q2 FY27 revenue rose 82% YoY to INR 120 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.83% and PAT declined about 27%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 120 crore, up 82% YoY, driven by order execution, but EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR 9 crore (7.83% margin) and PAT fell about 27% to INR 6 crore (5.08% margin). H1 FY27 revenue grew 62% to INR 196 crore, while H1 EBITDA rose about 5% to INR 16 crore (8.06%) and PAT rose about 6% to INR 11 crore (5.46%). Management attributed margin pressure to low-margin third-party product and project execution, higher freight (almost doubled), forex on fixed-price tariff-based contracts, employee and overhead costs, and start-up costs at the new Jhajjar (BESS) and Bakrol (UPS) plants. Management now guides to INR 500 crore FY27 revenue and an EBITDA margin above 11%, down from the earlier 13-14% range.

segments.name: BESS, EPC and developer projects
segments.commentary: About INR 909 crore of order book, roughly 81% of the total. Includes a INR 854 crore BESS developer order carrying annual rental of INR 62 crore over 12 years; management is in talks to down-sell two developer projects.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: INR 178 crore order book, around 16%. Management says it will be taken on a very selective basis going forward.

segments.name: Manufactured power solutions (UPS)
segments.commentary: INR 26 crore order book. Bakrol, Gujarat UPS plant (1 kVA to 600 kVA) began operations on September 25, 2026; management cites capacity of around INR 500-600 crore a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target around INR 500 crore: INR 266 crore order in hand plus INR 25-30 crore from channel, on top of H1 revenue of about INR 196-200 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin to be above 11%, with PAT in absolute terms expected to grow; percentage PAT growth expected to be difficult.
FY28 minimum revenue growth guidance of 25%, with EBITDA margin returning to 12-13% and PAT margin of 8.5-9%.
Jhajjar BESS plant capacity is 1.2 GWh on a single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts from FY28; FY28 BESS utilisation expected at 25-30%.
BESS revenue target of about INR 90 crore in FY27, from INR 54 crore of new orders plus INR 36 crore built in the current year.
Management expects working capital debt and total debt to rise in FY27 to support inventory and BESS needs; operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year end (not guaranteed).
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana 1.2 GWh BESS assembly facility commenced operations in Q2 FY27; management estimates around INR 1,000 crore a year at full single-shift utilisation.
Bakrol, Gujarat UPS assembly plant (about 3,000 pieces per day, single-phase, with lithium integration) commenced operations on September 25, 2026.
Peak utilisation of the new plants is expected in about 3 years, with the Jhajjar BESS plant focused on C&I rather than utilities.
Lithium cells will continue to be imported; in-house assembly is expected to reduce third-party dependency.
A sample 16 kW home energy storage system was exported in October 2026; export volumes depend on sample approval.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR 1,121 crore across 97 ongoing projects as of September 30, 2026; government customers about 78% and private about 22%, though management says most billing in H1 came from private customers.
Additional BESS order of 33 MWh received from new customers, alongside existing customers Adani Electricity, Bihar State Power and Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation.
Freight costs have almost doubled versus last year; forex moves hurt margins on fixed-price, tariff-based contracts.
Management says the market is becoming commoditised, with new entrants cutting prices and Chinese suppliers raising prices; differentiation is expected from local content.
Strategy shift: stopped direct government bidding for tenders up to INR 5 crore and is targeting selective high-value tenders and private C&I work through partner channels.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13-14% FY27 EBITDA margin guidance still achievable, and what is the H2 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now says FY27 EBITDA margin will be above 11% on about INR 500 crore revenue, with moderation expected in H2 but margins still on the higher side in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days are around 100, or about 178 days excluding one large September billing. Receivables fell from INR 257 crore at H1 to INR 201 crore in October after INR 73-75 crore of collections, with two large collections expected by December.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow was negative INR 49 crore at March 2026 and about negative INR 17 crore at September 2026. Management aims for positive by year end but cited capex and inventory build-up.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BESS developer project down-sell progressing, and what are the returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in talks with 6-7 players to down-sell two developer projects, and says equity IRR is above 12-13%. Margin could be lower than the original plan because of lithium, DC block and dollar cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company competitive in larger BESS projects and what differentiates it in a commoditising market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will focus on a few high-value tenders and C&I and says local domestic content will be the differentiator; it is positioning as an OEM and technology partner rather than as an EPC.

risks_watch: Margin compression: the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance fell from 13-14% to above 11%, and FY28 recovery to 12-13% depends on overhead absorption and cost easing.
Working capital and debt: working capital cycle at 192 days, inventory of about INR 120 crore, and debt expected to rise; operating cash flow still negative at H1.
Execution of the INR 500 crore FY27 revenue target requires about INR 300 crore of revenue from H2, against INR 266 crore order in hand plus channel business.
Pending down-sale of two BESS developer projects (INR 854 crore order) and its margin impact, with no timeline given.
Lithium cell import dependence and currency exposure; BESS utilisation of 25-30% in FY28 with a long-term peak in about 3 years.
Governance and disclosure: several analyst questions relied on unclear transcript points; management declined to name export customers or state steady-state PAT margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order book but defensive on margins; management repeatedly described the H1 margin fall as temporary while revising FY27 margin guidance down to above 11% and giving only broad, hedged answers on cash flow, down-sale timing and steady-state margins.

So, 25% is the minimum expectation that we are keeping an eye on next financial year.
So, today, whoever has stock is the king.
As of now, since we are coming up with the Jhajjar facility which we have come up.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to around INR 500 crore (H1 about INR 196-200 crore, backed by INR 266 crore order in hand plus INR 25-30 crore channel), with FY28 minimum 25% growth; but FY27 EBITDA margin cut to above 11% and FY28 BESS utilisation guided only 25-30%, and the market is commoditising.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut from 13-14% to above 11% and Q2 margin fell to 7.83% (H1 8.06%); FY28 recovery to 12-13% is guided but depends on overhead absorption and cost easing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant commenced in Q2 FY27 and Bakrol UPS plant began operations on Sept 25, 2026; scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts from FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to around INR 500 crore vs H1 about INR 196-200 crore, backed by INR 266 crore order in hand plus INR 25-30 crore channel; FY28 minimum 25% growth guided, though BESS utilisation is only 25-30%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Both new plants just commissioned with peak utilisation about 3 years away and FY28 BESS utilisation guided at only 25-30%; no new capex was announced, and the company is cash-constrained (operating cash flow about negative INR 17 crore at Sept 2026).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was cut to above 11% from 13-14%, and PAT percentage growth is expected to be difficult, so no upward revision is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue needs about INR 300 crore from H2 against INR 266 crore order in hand plus channel, and the INR 854 crore BESS developer order may be down-sold at lower margin with no timeline.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A 16 kW home energy storage sample was exported in October 2026, with export volumes dependent on sample approval; no launch date or volume was given.

rows.label: BESS developer order 33 MWh and INR 909 crore BESS/EPC/developer order book
rows.why: Order book of about INR 1,121 crore (81% in BESS, EPC and developer projects) across 97 projects, with an extra 33 MWh BESS order from new customers, supports revenue visibility.

rows.label: Receivables collection and cash flow turn positive
rows.why: Receivables fell from INR 257 crore to INR 201 crore in October after INR 73-75 crore collections with two large collections due by December, but operating cash flow was about negative INR 17 crore at Sept 2026 and management says positive turn is not guaranteed; working capital cycle is 192 days.

rows.label: Debt rise in FY27
rows.why: Management expects working capital and total debt to rise in FY27 to fund inventory (about INR 120 crore) and BESS needs, so leverage will not fall near term.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, INR 500 crore FY27 revenue and FY28 25% growth, but defensive on margins (guidance cut to above 11%) and hedged on cash flow, down-sell timing and steady-state margins; analysts pressed on margin trajectory, receivables and working capital.
